item.title: Heat-Wave Effects on Pregnant Women to Be Part of the COP31 Agenda
item.description: In the ramp-up to the United Nations annual climate change conference in November, alarming and under-reported statistics on the effects of climate change on maternal health and pregnancy are being pushed to the fore of discussions. item.title: France’s New Protest Generation Rises
item.description: Classrooms with mouldy walls, riddled with cockroaches and rats, stifling in summer and freezing in winter: this is how French high school students describe the places where they’re meant to learn. item.title: Security Council LIVE: Children and war, ‘each one is a life’
item.description: With violations against children caught in armed conflict reaching an unprecedented level this year, the Security Council is marking 30 years since it took on the mandate to protect young people caught up in war.

item.title: In Egypt, Guterres warns against Iran-US escalation
item.description: UN Secretary-General António Guterres called for dialogue and diplomacy to end the war between Iran and the United States in remarks on Monday to journalists in Cairo, Egypt.

item.title: Ebola: UN officials condemn killing of nurse in DR Congo
item.description: The UN’s Ebola coordinator and the head of the World Health Organization (WHO) have deplored the killing of a nurse working to halt the spread of the disease in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC).

item.title: West Bank: Hebron crackdown displaces thousands, Türk warns of ethnic cleansing
item.description: Israel’s “aggressive operation” in the West Bank city of Hebron raises serious concerns of ethnic cleansing, UN human rights chief Volker Türk warned on Monday, as the number of Palestinians forced from their homes passed 3,000 on the eve of Israeli elections.

item.title: Women and girls’ share of civilian war deaths doubles since 2021
item.description: War is growing deadlier for women and girls, who accounted for one in four of the more than 37,000 civilians killed in armed conflict last year – double their share in 2021 – according to major UN report released Monday.

item.title: Ukraine: Investigators find Russia committed war crimes by targeting civilians
item.description: Top human rights experts investigating Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine said on Monday that the Russian authorities had committed war crimes and crimes against humanity by attacking civilians and vital energy infrastructure, among other violations of international law.

item.title: How Conflict Brings Biodiversity to the Brink
item.description: Armenia-Azerbaijan's border forests, a biodiversity hotspot, are being transformed by militarisation, fear, and environmental loss. Experts say the same pattern is unfolding in conflict zones from Lebanon to Ukraine.

item.title: Upholding Human Rights & Public Safety: How Far Is Bangladesh?
